## Document: README.md (Overview)

# @actdim/msgmesh-remote

> **Bidirectional remote transport, WebSocket bridge, and reconnect orchestration for `@actdim/msgmesh`**

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@actdim/msgmesh-remote.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@actdim/msgmesh-remote)
[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.9+-blue.svg)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)

---

## What is MsgMesh Remote?

**`@actdim/msgmesh-remote`** carries [`@actdim/msgmesh`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@actdim/msgmesh) messages across a network boundary. A client bus (browser, WebView) and a server bus exchange the same `{ channel, group, topic, payload }` messages over one duplex socket, using a small typed JSON frame protocol.

### The Problem It Solves
- **Two buses, one app**: the UI talks to a local msgmesh bus, the server publishes on its own; something has to move events and RPC calls between them.
- **Dead mobile sockets**: WebViews (.NET MAUI, iOS WKWebView, Android WebView) can leave a WebSocket half-open after the app is suspended, with no `close` event.
- **Lost state on reconnect**: subscriptions and messages sent during a short outage vanish unless the transport replays them.

### The Output You Get
- **Full-Duplex Wire Protocol**: strongly typed frames `SUB`, `UNSUB`, `MSG`, `REQ`, `RES`, `PING`, `PONG`, `AUTH`, `AUTH_OK`, `AUTH_FAIL`, with a validating JSON codec and a pluggable `FrameCodec`.
- **Framework-Agnostic Server**: `RemoteMeshServer` works with any socket that matches the duck-typed `RemoteSocket` contract - `ws` / `@fastify/websocket`, or a custom implementation. The frames are plain JSON, so other server stacks can implement the same protocol.
- **Resilient Client**: `RemoteMeshClient` sends a heartbeat every 15 s and treats a `PONG` missing for 5 s as a dead socket, then reconnects with exponential backoff and jitter.
- **Auto-Resubscription**: active channel/topic subscriptions are replayed after every reconnect.
- **Offline Message Buffer**: bounded queue (200 by default) for outbound fire-and-forget messages sent while disconnected.
- **RPC Correlation**: `client.request()` maps requests to correlated responses with timeouts; `bridgeRemoteBus` exposes remote channels as local `bus.request()` providers.
- **Security Hooks**: handshake context, in-band `AUTH` / token refresh (`client.authenticate(token)`), per-frame `authorize`, per-session `filterEvent` with a default owner-based tenant filter.

---

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @actdim/msgmesh-remote @actdim/msgmesh rxjs
```

Peer dependencies: `@actdim/msgmesh >=1.12.0`, `rxjs >=7.8.0`. ESM only.

| Entry point | Contents |
|---|---|
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/client` | `RemoteMeshClient`, `bridgeRemoteBus` |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/server` | `RemoteMeshServer`, `RemoteClientSession` |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/protocol` | `JsonFrameCodec`, `defaultCodec`, `validateFrame`, `create*Frame` factories, error classes |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote` | All of the above plus the type contracts |

---

## Quick Start

### Server (Node.js, `@fastify/websocket`)

```typescript
import { RemoteMeshServer, type RemoteSocket } from '@actdim/msgmesh-remote/server';

const remoteServer = new RemoteMeshServer({
    bus: serverBus, // your msgmesh bus
    onAuthenticate: async (token) => {
        const user = await verifyToken(token);
        return user ? { userId: user.id } : null;
    },
});

fastify.get('/api/v1/ws', { websocket: true }, (socket) => {
    remoteServer.handleConnection(socket as unknown as RemoteSocket);
});

// server code publishes as usual; subscribed clients receive it
await serverBus.send({ channel: 'JOBS.STATUS', topic: jobId, payload: { jobId, progress: 55 } });
```

### Client (browser / WebView)

```typescript
import { RemoteMeshClient, bridgeRemoteBus, type RemoteBusLike } from '@actdim/msgmesh-remote/client';

const client = new RemoteMeshClient({
    url: 'wss://example.com/api/v1/ws',
    tokenGetter: () => getAccessToken(),
});

// incoming events are re-published on the local bus
const unbridge = bridgeRemoteBus(appBus as unknown as RemoteBusLike, client, {
    remoteSubscriptions: [{ channel: 'WORKS.INTAKE.*' }],
});

client.connect();
client.subscribe('JOBS.STATUS', jobId);

appBus.on({ channel: 'JOBS.STATUS', topic: jobId, callback: (msg) => render(msg.payload) });

// direct RPC to the server bus
const doc = await client.request<{ name: string }>('CAD.GET_DOCUMENT', { id: 'doc-001' });
```

`serverBus`, `appBus`, `verifyToken`, `getAccessToken` and `render` are application code. With a msgmesh server bus, wildcard channel subscriptions such as `WORKS.INTAKE.*` need `resolveChannels` on the server - see the [Integration Guide](./docs/topic--04-integration-guide.md).

# ALONG-PROTOCOL v4.6.0

This repo carries its own agent context, provider-agnostically. Follow it every session, whatever tool you are. This is the core; procedures (completion checklist, doc routing, merges, along-team, tool-use rules) live in `docs/topic--along-protocol.md` - pull the section you need via `/along-kb-search`. A gate's error message carries its detail.

## Where state lives
- **Nearest wins**: any folder may carry its own `AGENTS.md` + `.along/`; use the NEAREST for the area you work in. Nearest `.along/` > higher-level `.along/` > global config. Only a nested `.git` or a user-run `along init` makes a subproject.
- **Read at session start** (not auto-loaded): `.along/ISSUES.md`, `.along/CONSTRAINTS.md`, your issue `.along/ISSUES/<type>--<slug>.md`; when relevant `.along/VISION.md`, `.along/GLOSSARY.md`. They reflect the state WHEN WRITTEN - verify named files/APIs/flags against the code.
- **Entities**: issues (`feat|bug|debt|task|docs|spike`), ADRs (`.along/DECISIONS/`, never edited - superseded), milestones, sessions. Keys `<type>--<slug>`, referenced by key, never by path; schemas in `docs/topic--domain-model.md`. Create them from intent unprompted (build/fix -> issue, blocked -> issue tagged `risk`, compare -> `spike` issue, release -> milestone).
- **Projections** (`ISSUES.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `CONSTRAINTS.md`, `docs/INDEX.md`) are compiled: on conflict take either side and re-run the sync.

## Anchor work to an issue
1. Find or create the issue with `status: in-progress`; `along start <slug>` binds this session.
2. Source edits unlock after the user approves the plan (`EnterPlanMode` -> `ExitPlanMode`, or `along plan approve --plan-file <path>` after their explicit yes). Questions get read-only answers; 1-line typo/comment edits are exempt.
3. Commit via `/along-commit`: bound to the slug, no AI `Co-Authored-By:` trailers.
4. Finish with the completion checklist, ending in `along wrap <slug> --summary "..." (--decisions <ADR...> | --no-decisions)`.

## Gates
Runtime hooks enforce these where installed; elsewhere (`along doctor` shows the level) self-apply every one and use the `along` CLI instead of raw tools.
- [gate: require-active-issue] [gate: require-plan-approval] - no source edit without an in-progress issue and an approved plan.
- [gate: subproject-boundary] - a subproject's entities go in ITS `.along/`; cross-subproject work needs an issue in each, or a root umbrella with `parent:` children.
- [gate: workspace-containment] - read/write inside the workspace (plus temp); other roots need `allowed_roots`; never credential stores.
- [gate: projection-protection] - never hand-edit or hand-merge projections.
- [gate: commit-issue-binding] - every commit names the active issue.
- [gate: issue-lifecycle] [gate: entity-reference-integrity] [gate: entity-deletion-protection] - close via `along wrap` / `along issue done`; rename or supersede, never delete a referenced entity.
- [gate: doc-manual-lock] - `write_policy: manual` docs change only under a `docs--<slug>` issue.
- [gate: rule-pack-protection] - never edit `.along/rules/**/*.md` (`along rules attach` owns them).
- [gate: doc-routing-compliance] - ADR vs `README.md` vs `docs/topic--*.md` routing tree.
- [gate: untracked-exports] - dashboards and `.along/diagnostics/` stay out of Git.
- [gate: cli_safety] - file content via file tools, never heredocs or `python -c`; no global installs.
- [gate: team-step-active] [gate: team-reviews-before-stop] - an `along-team` blackboard holds you to its step loop.
- [gate: test_before_stop] [gate: wrap_before_stop] [gate: projection_sync_before_stop] - before stopping: tests run after your last edit, session wrapped, projections synced.
- [gate: unresolved_gate_denial] - a denied tool call is redone within the gate's rules or told to the user (`along gates ack`), never dropped silently; closing waits for their reply.
- Commit-time (`along lint`, pre-commit + CI): ASCII typography, fence languages, relative links, no `docs/` -> `.along/` links, Windows-safe names, no secrets, no stubs.
- Bypass is the user's call: `-n`, `--force-reason`, `scratch fallback` need `--reason` after their reply; recorded in `along gates stats`.

## Judgment rules
- Ground facts in code, `README.md` and `docs/`; no generic placeholders. Query `/along-kb-search` before reading whole docs; update affected `docs/topic--*.md` after non-trivial changes.
- Use `/along-test`, `/along-build`, `/along-dev` before raw commands, with quiet flags. Review your diff and blast radius (`along graph-impact`).
- Never delete or truncate docs, comments or code unless told; no stubs; check `git diff --stat` after batch edits. Verify written files parse. Tests stay hermetic.
- Stay in scope: failures your issue did not cause (red at HEAD, untouched code) are reported and filed as an issue, never fixed under this one; never edit tests or fixtures to make them pass unless the issue is about them; bypass (`-n --reason`) only after the user's reply.
- Scope > 3 files, crossing subsystems or refactoring core engines: route to `along-team`; plans MUST declare `Execution Mode: Direct` or `Role-Based`.
- Treat the `along` CLI as a black box (`along <cmd> --help`, no engine source outside the Along repo); report its errors verbatim.

## Project specifics

<!-- BEGIN ALONG-RULES -->
See the following engineering guidelines:
- `[languages/typescript.md](.along/rules/languages/typescript.md)`
- `[platforms/web.md](.along/rules/platforms/web.md)`
<!-- END ALONG-RULES -->

- **Package**: `@actdim/msgmesh-remote` - bidirectional remote transport for `@actdim/msgmesh`: a JSON frame protocol (`SUB`, `UNSUB`, `MSG`, `REQ`, `RES`, `PING`, `PONG`, `AUTH`, `AUTH_OK`, `AUTH_FAIL`), a framework-agnostic `RemoteMeshServer` (sessions over a duck-typed `RemoteSocket`, mapped onto a server bus) and a resilient `RemoteMeshClient` (heartbeat, backoff reconnect, subscription replay, offline queue, correlated RPC) with `bridgeRemoteBus` to wire it into a local bus.
- **Entry points**: `.` (everything, `src/index.ts`), `./client` (`src/client.ts`), `./server` (`src/server.ts`), `./protocol` (`src/protocol.ts`, values only); type contracts in `src/types.ts` (reachable as `./types` via the `./*` export). ESM only. Peers: `@actdim/msgmesh >=1.12.0`, `rxjs >=7.8.0`; the runtime never imports msgmesh, it uses the structural `RemoteBusLike` / `RemoteServerBusLike` interfaces.
- **Commands** (package folder): `pnpm run build` (`tsc -b tsconfig.json && vite build`), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run test` (Vitest, `vitest.node.config.ts`, hermetic in-memory sockets in `tests/`), `pnpm run docs:build` (VitePress).
- **Knowledge Base**: `docs/INDEX.md` (overview, core concepts, architecture and wiring, integration guide, API reference, domain model, setup). Consumers in mempart: `apps/server/src/controllers/ws/wsController.ts`, `apps/webapp/src/config/remoteClient.ts`.
- **Versioning**: developed as a submodule of the mempart pnpm monorepo (`src/packages/msgmesh-remote`) under one unified version. Never bump `package.json` here in isolation; versions change only via mempart `pnpm run version:sync <version>` (from mempart `src/`), committed, tagged and pushed together with the root repo and all submodules.

## Document: docs/topic--01-overview-and-advantages.md (Overview & Key Advantages)

# Overview & Key Advantages

[<- Back to README](../README.md) | [Next: 02. Core Concepts ->](./topic--02-core-concepts.md)

---

## What is @actdim/msgmesh-remote?

**`@actdim/msgmesh-remote`** extends an in-process [`@actdim/msgmesh`](https://actdim.github.io/msgmesh/) bus across a network boundary. A browser (or WebView) bus and a server bus exchange the same `{ channel, group, topic, payload }` messages over one duplex socket, using a small JSON frame protocol.

The package has three parts, each published as its own entry point:

- **Protocol** (`@actdim/msgmesh-remote/protocol`) - the frame vocabulary (`SUB`, `UNSUB`, `MSG`, `REQ`, `RES`, `PING`, `PONG`, `AUTH`, `AUTH_OK`, `AUTH_FAIL`), a validating JSON codec (`JsonFrameCodec`, `defaultCodec`) and frame factory functions.
- **Client** (`@actdim/msgmesh-remote/client`) - `RemoteMeshClient`, a resilient connection with heartbeat, exponential reconnect, subscription replay, an offline send queue and correlated RPC; plus `bridgeRemoteBus` to wire it into a local bus declaratively.
- **Server** (`@actdim/msgmesh-remote/server`) - `RemoteMeshServer`, a framework-agnostic session manager that maps client frames onto a server-side bus, with hooks for authentication, authorization, channel resolution and per-session event filtering.

The root entry point (`@actdim/msgmesh-remote`) re-exports all three plus the shared type contracts.

---

## Where It Fits

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Browser["Browser / WebView"]
        UI["UI components"] --> CBUS["msgmesh bus (client)"]
        CBUS <--> BR["bridgeRemoteBus"]
        BR <--> CL["RemoteMeshClient"]
    end
    CL <-- "JSON frames over WebSocket" --> SV["RemoteMeshServer"]
    subgraph Server["Node.js server"]
        SV --> SESS["RemoteClientSession (per socket)"]
        SESS <--> SBUS["msgmesh bus (server)"]
        SBUS <--> SVC["Domain services / job watchers"]
    end
```

UI code keeps talking only to its local bus. Remote delivery, reconnects and authentication are concerns of the transport layer, not of components.

---

## Key Advantages

### 1. One Messaging Model End to End
- Frames carry the same `channel` / `group` / `topic` addressing that `@actdim/msgmesh` uses in-process, so a server event can land on the client bus unchanged and be consumed with a normal `bus.on(...)`.
- RPC across the wire is a plain `client.request(channel, payload)` on the client and a plain `bus.request(...)` provider on the server.

### 2. Transport Agnostic
- The server depends only on the duck-typed `RemoteSocket` contract (`send`, `on('message' | 'close' | 'error')`, `close`). A `ws` socket from `@fastify/websocket` satisfies it directly; so does an in-memory socket pair in tests.
- The client accepts a URL (string or getter) for the global `WebSocket`, or a `socketFactory` returning either a DOM-style `WebSocket` or any `RemoteSocket`.
- Serialization is pluggable through the `FrameCodec` interface.

### 3. Built for Flaky Mobile Connections
- Client heartbeat: a `PING` every 15 s (`heartbeatIntervalMs`) and a 5 s `PONG` deadline (`heartbeatTimeoutMs`); a missed `PONG` terminates the half-open socket and reconnects. This targets WebViews (.NET MAUI, iOS WKWebView, Android WebView) where a suspended app can leave a socket silently dead.
- Reconnect with exponential backoff (factor 1.5, 500 ms -> 10 s by default) and +/-20% jitter.
- Subscriptions are kept in a registry and replayed after every reconnect; fire-and-forget sends made while offline are buffered (200 frames by default) and flushed in order.

### 4. Security Hooks at the Session Boundary
- Handshake context (`handleConnection(socket, { userId, metadata })`) plus in-band `AUTH` frames for login and token refresh without reconnecting (`client.authenticate(token)`).
- `authorize(context, frame)` gates every non-`AUTH` frame; a denied `REQ` gets a `403` error response.
- Per-session event filtering (`filterEvent`), with a built-in default that drops events whose payload `userId` / `ownerUserId` belongs to another user.

### 5. Small, Dependency-Light
- Runtime code is five source files; `@actdim/msgmesh` and `rxjs` are peer dependencies only. The client and server talk to "bus-like" structural interfaces (`RemoteBusLike`, `RemoteServerBusLike`), so a msgmesh bus fits without adapters and tests can pass plain object mocks.

---

## Real-World Usage (mempart)

Inside the mempart monorepo the package connects the web app to the Fastify server:

- **Server**: `apps/server/src/controllers/ws/wsController.ts` creates a `RemoteMeshServer<ServerChannel, 'in'>` over the server bus, registers it on `/api/v1/ws` and `/ws`, verifies tokens in `onAuthenticate`, starts job watching from `authorize` when a client subscribes to `JOBS.STATUS`, and enforces tenant isolation in `filterEvent`.
- **Client**: `apps/webapp/src/config/remoteClient.ts` creates a `RemoteMeshClient` with a `tokenGetter` that asks the app bus for the current access token, bridges it to the app bus with `bridgeRemoteBus` (`WORKS.INTAKE.*`, `FEED.EXCHANGE.*`, `JOBS.STATUS`, `VFS.DRIVE.SYNC_STATUS`, `VFS.NODE.*`), and re-authenticates on `APP.SECURITY.AUTH.SIGNIN`.

See [04. Integration Guide](./topic--04-integration-guide.md) for the full wiring.

## Document: docs/topic--02-core-concepts.md (Core Concepts)

# Core Concepts

[<- Back to 01. Overview](./topic--01-overview-and-advantages.md) | [Next: 03. Architecture & Wiring ->](./topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md)

---

## 1. Addressing: Channel, Group, Topic

`@actdim/msgmesh` addresses every message by **channel** (for example `JOBS.STATUS`), **group** (`in`, `out`, `ex`, ... - the payload role; msgmesh defaults to `in`) and optional **topic** (a sub-stream key such as a job id). The remote protocol carries exactly these three fields on `SUB`, `UNSUB`, `MSG` and `REQ` frames, so a frame maps one-to-one onto a bus call:

| Frame field | Bus field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `channel` | `channel` | Required, non-empty string |
| `group` | `group` | Optional; omitted means the bus default group |
| `topic` | `topic` | Optional; `'*'` in a `SUB` means "every topic" |
| `payload` | `payload` | Optional; any JSON-serializable value |

### Wildcards in subscriptions

A client subscription is a `{ channel, topic?, group? }` triple. The server matches incoming bus events against it with `RemoteClientSession.isSubscribed(channel, topic?, group?)`:

- **Channel**: `'*'` matches everything; a trailing `*` is a prefix match (`'WORKS.INTAKE.*'` matches `WORKS.INTAKE.COMPLETED`); anything else is exact.
- **Topic / group**: missing or `'*'` matches any value; anything else is exact.

The server must also *listen* on concrete bus channels. A msgmesh bus has no channel wildcards, so a prefix subscription needs `RemoteServerOptions.resolveChannels(pattern)` to expand the pattern into the list of real channels (see "Server subscription pipeline" in [03. Architecture & Wiring](./topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md)).

---

## 2. Frames

All traffic is a stream of frames discriminated by the `t` field. Shapes are defined in `src/types.ts` and validated by `validateFrame` in `src/protocol.ts`.

| `t` | Direction | Purpose | Required fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SUB` | client -> server | Start receiving events for an address | `channel` |
| `UNSUB` | client -> server | Stop receiving events for an address | `channel` |
| `MSG` | both | Fire-and-forget message / event | `channel` |
| `REQ` | client -> server | Correlated RPC request | `id`, `channel` |
| `RES` | server -> client | RPC response (`payload` or `error`) | `id` |
| `PING` | both | Heartbeat probe | - |
| `PONG` | both | Heartbeat answer | - |
| `AUTH` | client -> server | Authenticate or refresh the token in-band | `token` (non-empty) |
| `AUTH_OK` | server -> client | Authentication accepted (optional `userId`) | - |
| `AUTH_FAIL` | server -> client | Authentication rejected (optional `code`) | `error` (non-empty) |

The full field-level contract is in [Domain Model](./topic--domain-model.md).

### Codec

A `FrameCodec` turns frames into wire data and back:

```typescript
export interface FrameCodec {
    encode(frame: RemoteFrame): string | Uint8Array;
    decode(raw: string | Uint8Array): RemoteFrame;
}
```

`JsonFrameCodec` (exported singleton: `defaultCodec`) encodes with `JSON.stringify`, decodes strings or `Uint8Array` (UTF-8 via `TextDecoder`), and validates the result. Bad JSON raises `FrameDecodeError`; a structurally invalid frame raises `InvalidFrameError`. Both the client and the server log decode failures and drop the frame instead of closing the connection.

---

## 3. The Bus-Like Contracts

Neither side imports the msgmesh runtime. They depend on structural interfaces that a msgmesh `MsgBus` already satisfies:

- **`RemoteServerBusLike`** (server side): optional `send(msg)`, `request(msg)` and `on({ channel, group?, topic?, options?: { abortSignal }, callback })`.
- **`RemoteBusLike`** (client side): everything above plus optional `provide({ channel, group?, callback })`.

Every method is optional; the code checks `typeof bus.x === 'function'` before calling. Missing `request` on the server produces an error `RES` (`'Server bus has no request provider'`); missing `send` or `on` turns the corresponding feature into a no-op.

---

## 4. Client Connection Lifecycle

`RemoteMeshClient` is a small state machine exposed through `getState()` and `onStateChange(listener)`:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> CLOSED
    CLOSED --> CONNECTING: connect() (first attempt)
    CONNECTING --> OPEN: socket open
    OPEN --> RECONNECTING: socket closed / PONG timeout
    RECONNECTING --> RECONNECTING: backoff timer -> connect()
    RECONNECTING --> OPEN: socket open
    OPEN --> CLOSED: close()
    CONNECTING --> CLOSED: close()
    RECONNECTING --> CLOSED: close()
```

On every transition to `OPEN` the client, in order:

1. resets the reconnect attempt counter and starts the heartbeat;
2. sends an `AUTH` frame if `options.token` or `await options.tokenGetter()` yields a token;
3. replays a `SUB` frame for every registered subscription;
4. flushes the offline queue.

The automatic `AUTH` on open is fire-and-forget: frames sent in steps 3-4 do not wait for `AUTH_OK`. Use the server's handshake context or `authorize` if early frames must already be authenticated.

### Socket flavours

- **DOM-style `WebSocket`** (has `addEventListener`): the client waits for the `open` event and unwraps `MessageEvent.data`.
- **`RemoteSocket`** (has `on`): the socket is treated as already open, and the open sequence runs immediately.

### Heartbeat

While `OPEN`, the client sends `PING` every `heartbeatIntervalMs` (default `15000`) and arms a `heartbeatTimeoutMs` timer (default `5000`). A `PONG` clears the timer; otherwise the client closes the socket and schedules a reconnect. The client also answers server `PING` frames with `PONG`. The server answers `PING` but never originates one.

### Reconnect backoff

```text
delay = min(minReconnectDelayMs * 1.5^(attempt - 1), maxReconnectDelayMs) * random(0.8 .. 1.2)
```

Defaults: `minReconnectDelayMs = 500`, `maxReconnectDelayMs = 10000`. Only an explicit `close()` stops reconnecting. A `url` given as a function is re-evaluated on each attempt, so it can embed a fresh token or host.

---

## 5. Subscriptions, Offline Queue and Requests

| Operation | While `OPEN` | While not `OPEN` |
|---|---|---|
| `subscribe(channel, topic?, group?)` | Registered and `SUB` sent | Registered; `SUB` sent on next open |
| `unsubscribe(channel, topic?, group?)` | Removed and `UNSUB` sent | Removed from the registry only |
| `send(channel, payload?, topic?, group?)` | `MSG` sent | Queued (FIFO, up to `maxOfflineQueueSize`, default `200`; overflow is dropped with a warning) |
| `request(channel, payload?, { topic?, group?, timeout? })` | `REQ` sent, awaits `RES` | Registered but **not sent and not queued**; rejects on timeout |

Subscription identity is the key `channel::group::topic`, so subscribing twice to the same address is idempotent.

`request()` generates an id (`req-<random>-<time>`), rejects with `Request timeout after <ms>ms` after `options.timeout ?? defaultRequestTimeoutMs ?? 10000`, resolves with `RES.payload`, and rejects with the raw `RES.error` value when the server reports an error. `close()` rejects every pending request and pending authentication with `Client connection closed` and clears the offline queue.

---

## 6. Authentication

Two mechanisms coexist:

- **Handshake context**: the host verifies credentials during the WebSocket upgrade (query string, header, cookie) and passes `{ userId, metadata }` to `server.handleConnection(socket, context)`.
- **In-band `AUTH`**: the client sends `AUTH` (automatically on open, or explicitly via `authenticate(token, timeoutMs = 10000)`). The server calls `onAuthenticate(token, context)`:

| `onAuthenticate` result | Server reply | Session effect |
|---|---|---|
| hook not configured | `AUTH_OK` with current `userId` | none |
| falsy (`null`, `false`) | `AUTH_FAIL` `'Authentication failed'`, code `401` | none |
| `true` | `AUTH_OK` with current `userId` | none |
| `{ userId?, metadata? }` | `AUTH_OK` with resulting `userId` | `userId` replaced, `metadata` shallow-merged |
| throws | `AUTH_FAIL` with the error message, code `500` | none |

`authenticate()` resolves on `AUTH_OK` and rejects on `AUTH_FAIL` or timeout; a newer call supersedes a pending one. It rejects immediately if the client is not `OPEN`.

---

## 7. Authorization and Event Filtering

- **`authorize(context, frame)`** runs for every inbound frame except `AUTH` (including `PING`). If it returns `false`, the frame is dropped; a denied `REQ` receives `RES` with `error: { message: 'Unauthorized', code: 403 }`.
- **`filterEvent(context, channel, payload, topic?, group?)`** decides per session whether a bus event is forwarded. Without it, the default filter drops an event when the payload has `userId` or `ownerUserId`, the session has a `userId`, and the two differ (compared as strings). Sessions without a `userId` receive everything under the default filter.
- **`server.broadcast(...)`** pushes directly to subscribed sessions and does not run `filterEvent`.

---

[<- Back to 01. Overview](./topic--01-overview-and-advantages.md) | [Next: 03. Architecture & Wiring ->](./topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md)

## Document: docs/topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md (Architecture & Wiring)

# Architecture & Wiring

[<- Back to 02. Core Concepts](./topic--02-core-concepts.md) | [Next: 04. Integration Guide ->](./topic--04-integration-guide.md)

---

## 1. Component Map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Client["Client process (browser / WebView)"]
        LBUS["Local bus (RemoteBusLike)"]
        BRIDGE["bridgeRemoteBus / client.attachToBus"]
        RMC["RemoteMeshClient"]
        LBUS -- "provide(remoteRequests)" --> BRIDGE
        BRIDGE -- "bus.send(MSG)" --> LBUS
        BRIDGE <--> RMC
    end
    subgraph Wire["Transport"]
        SOCK["WebSocket or RemoteSocket + FrameCodec"]
    end
    subgraph Server["Server process"]
        RMS["RemoteMeshServer"]
        SES["RemoteClientSession (1 per socket)"]
        SBUS["Server bus (RemoteServerBusLike)"]
        RMS -- "handleConnection" --> SES
        SES -- "send / request / on" --> SBUS
    end
    RMC <--> SOCK <--> SES
```

| Unit | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Frame types, socket and bus contracts | `src/types.ts` | Pure type declarations |
| Codec, validation, frame factories | `src/protocol.ts` | `JsonFrameCodec`, `validateFrame`, `create*Frame` |
| `RemoteMeshServer`, `RemoteClientSession` | `src/server.ts` | Session registry, frame dispatch, bus listeners, auth hooks |
| `RemoteMeshClient`, `bridgeRemoteBus` | `src/client.ts` | Connection state, heartbeat, reconnect, queue, RPC, bus bridge |

---

## 2. Connection Open, Auth and Resubscribe

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Client app
    participant C as RemoteMeshClient
    participant S as RemoteClientSession
    participant H as Server hooks
    App->>C: connect()
    Note over C: state CONNECTING (or RECONNECTING)
    C->>S: socket open (handleConnection(socket, context))
    Note over C: state OPEN, heartbeat started
    C->>S: AUTH { token } (if token / tokenGetter)
    S->>H: onAuthenticate(token, context)
    H-->>S: { userId, metadata } | true | falsy
    S-->>C: AUTH_OK { userId } or AUTH_FAIL { error, code }
    C->>S: SUB { channel, topic?, group? } (replay of every registered subscription)
    C->>S: MSG ... (offline queue flush, FIFO)
```

`AUTH`, `SUB` and the queued `MSG` frames are written back to back. On the server each frame is dispatched as `void session.handleFrame(frame)`, so an `onAuthenticate` that awaits I/O can still be running when the following `SUB` frames are processed.

---

## 3. Remote RPC (client -> server)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant UI as UI code
    participant LB as Local bus
    participant BR as bridgeRemoteBus provider
    participant C as RemoteMeshClient
    participant S as RemoteClientSession
    participant SB as Server bus
    UI->>LB: request({ channel: 'API.REMOTE.CALL', payload })
    LB->>BR: provider callback(inMsg)
    BR->>C: request(channel, inMsg.payload, { topic, group })
    C->>S: REQ { id, channel, topic?, group?, payload }
    S->>S: authorize(context, frame)?
    S->>SB: request({ channel, group, topic, payload })
    SB-->>S: response (msgmesh Msg or raw value)
    S-->>C: RES { id, payload } or RES { id, error }
    C-->>BR: resolve(payload) / reject(error)
    BR-->>LB: provider result
    LB-->>UI: response
```

- Only channels listed in `RemoteBusBridgeConfig.remoteRequests` (array form) get a local `provide()` registration. The topic and group are taken from `inMsg.address` (falling back to `inMsg.topic` / `inMsg.group`).
- On the server, a response object that has a `payload` property (a msgmesh response message) is unwrapped to that `payload`; any other value is sent as-is.
- A thrown error becomes `RES.error`: for an `Error` instance `{ message, name, ...ownEnumerableProps }`, for another object its own enumerable props, otherwise `{ message: String(err) }`.
- `client.request()` can also be called directly without the bridge.

---

## 4. Server Events to the Client (pub/sub)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as RemoteMeshClient
    participant S as RemoteClientSession
    participant SB as Server bus
    participant SVC as Server service
    participant LB as Client local bus
    C->>S: SUB { channel: 'WORKS.INTAKE.*' }
    S->>S: resolveChannels('WORKS.INTAKE.*') -> concrete channels
    S->>SB: on({ channel, topic, options: { abortSignal }, callback }) per channel
    SVC->>SB: send({ channel: 'WORKS.INTAKE.RECEIVED', payload })
    SB-->>S: callback(msg)
    S->>S: isSubscribed(channel, topic, group) and filterEvent / default owner filter
    S-->>C: MSG { channel, topic?, group?, payload }
    C->>C: onMessage listeners
    C->>LB: bus.send({ channel, group, topic, payload }) (via bridge)
```

### Server subscription pipeline

For a `SUB` frame, `RemoteClientSession`:

1. Stores the subscription under `channel::group::topic`.
2. Computes the bus channels to listen on: `resolveChannels(frame.channel)` if configured, otherwise `[frame.channel]` verbatim.
3. For each bus channel not yet listened on (keyed by `busChannel::topic`), calls `bus.on({ channel, topic, options: { abortSignal }, callback })`. A topic of `'*'` is translated to the msgmesh regex topic `'/.*/'`. No `group` is passed, so a msgmesh bus listens on its default group (`in`), which is also the group `bus.send` uses when none is given.
4. In the callback, reads `channel` / `topic` / `group` from `msg.address` (or top-level fields), takes `msg.payload` (or the whole message if there is none), re-checks `isSubscribed`, applies `filterEvent` (or the default owner filter) and sends a `MSG` frame.

Two consequences for a msgmesh server bus:

- **Channel wildcards need `resolveChannels`.** Without it, `SUB 'WORKS.INTAKE.*'` makes the session listen on a bus channel literally named `WORKS.INTAKE.*`.
- **Topic-less subscriptions only see topic-less events.** msgmesh matches an undefined listener topic only against messages without a topic, so to receive `JOBS.STATUS` events published with `topic: jobId`, subscribe with that topic (or with `'*'`).

`UNSUB` removes the stored subscription and aborts a bus listener only when no remaining subscription resolves to the same bus channel and topic. Closing the socket (`close` or `error` event) calls `session.close()`, which aborts every bus listener and removes the session from the server.

### Server-initiated pushes

`server.broadcast(channel, payload?, topic?, group?)` sends a `MSG` to every session whose subscriptions match, independent of the server bus.

---

## 5. Client Messages to the Server (fire-and-forget)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Client app
    participant C as RemoteMeshClient
    participant S as RemoteClientSession
    participant SB as Server bus
    App->>C: send('CAD.OBJECT_MUTATION', payload)
    alt state OPEN
        C->>S: MSG { channel, payload }
    else not OPEN
        C->>C: offlineQueue.push (max maxOfflineQueueSize)
        Note over C: flushed after next open
        C->>S: MSG { channel, payload }
    end
    S->>S: authorize(context, frame)?
    S->>SB: send({ channel, group, topic, payload })
```

---

## 6. Heartbeat and Reconnect

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as RemoteMeshClient
    participant S as RemoteClientSession
    loop every heartbeatIntervalMs (15000)
        C->>S: PING
        alt PONG within heartbeatTimeoutMs (5000)
            S-->>C: PONG
        else timeout
            C->>C: close socket, state RECONNECTING
            C->>C: wait min(min * 1.5^(n-1), max) * jitter
            C->>S: new socket, open sequence (AUTH, SUB replay, queue flush)
        end
    end
```

---

## 7. Declarative Bridge

`bridgeRemoteBus(bus, client, config)` (or `client.attachToBus(bus, config)`) wires three things and returns one disposer:

| Config field | Effect |
|---|---|
| `remoteSubscriptions: RemoteSubscriptionItem[]` | `client.subscribe(...)` for each item now; `client.unsubscribe(...)` on dispose |
| `remoteRequests: TChannel[]` | `bus.provide({ channel, callback })` forwarding to `client.request(...)`; provider disposed on dispose |
| *(always)* | `client.onMessage` -> `bus.send({ channel, group, topic, payload })` for every incoming `MSG` |

`RemoteBusBridgeConfig` also declares `remoteRequests` as a predicate function and a `sendToRemote` field; neither is acted on by `bridgeRemoteBus` in the current source (only the array form of `remoteRequests` registers providers, and local-to-remote forwarding is done by calling `client.send` yourself).

---

# Integration Guide

[<- Back to 03. Architecture & Wiring](./topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md) | [Next: 05. API Reference ->](./topic--05-api-reference.md)

---

## 1. Installation

```bash
pnpm add @actdim/msgmesh-remote @actdim/msgmesh rxjs
```

| Peer dependency | Range |
|---|---|
| `@actdim/msgmesh` | `>=1.12.0` |
| `rxjs` | `>=7.8.0` |

The package is ESM-only (`"type": "module"`) and side-effect free. Import from the narrowest entry point you need:

| Import path | Use in | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/client` | Browser / WebView | `RemoteMeshClient`, `bridgeRemoteBus`, client option and bridge types |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/server` | Node.js server | `RemoteMeshServer`, `RemoteClientSession`, server option and context types |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/protocol` | Either side, tools, tests | Codec, validation, error classes, `create*Frame` factories |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/types` | Either side | All frame, codec, socket and bus-like type contracts (via the `./*` export) |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote` | Either side | Everything above |

---

## 2. Server: Fastify + @fastify/websocket

`@fastify/websocket` hands each route a `ws` socket, which already matches the `RemoteSocket` contract (`send`, `on('message' | 'close' | 'error')`, `close`). This is condensed from mempart's `apps/server/src/controllers/ws/wsController.ts`:

```typescript
import { type FastifyInstance, type FastifyRequest } from 'fastify';
import {
    RemoteMeshServer,
    type RemoteSocket,
    type RemoteConnectionContext,
    type RemoteFrame,
} from '@actdim/msgmesh-remote/server';

export function wsController(fastify: FastifyInstance): RemoteMeshServer<ServerChannel, 'in'> {
    const remoteServer = new RemoteMeshServer<ServerChannel, 'in'>({
        bus: serverBus, // a msgmesh MsgBus
        // msgmesh has no channel wildcards: expand 'WORKS.INTAKE.*' into concrete channels
        resolveChannels: (pattern: string): ServerChannel[] => {
            if (pattern === '*' || pattern.endsWith('*')) {
                const prefix = pattern === '*' ? '' : pattern.slice(0, -1);
                return knownChannels.filter((ch) => ch.startsWith(prefix));
            }
            const exact = pattern as ServerChannel;
            return knownChannels.includes(exact) ? [exact] : [];
        },
        // in-band AUTH frames
        onAuthenticate: async (token: string) => {
            const auth = await verifyRemoteToken(token, fastify);
            if (!auth) return null; // -> AUTH_FAIL 401
            return { userId: auth.userId, metadata: { roles: auth.roles, email: auth.email } };
        },
        // runs for every non-AUTH frame
        authorize: async (context: RemoteConnectionContext, frame: RemoteFrame) => true,
        // per-session event visibility
        filterEvent: (context: RemoteConnectionContext, _channel: string, payload: unknown): boolean => {
            if (!context.userId) return false;
            const record = payload as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
            const owner = record?.ownerUserId ?? record?.userId;
            return owner === undefined || String(owner) === String(context.userId);
        },
    });

    fastify.get('/api/v1/ws', { websocket: true }, async (socket: unknown, request: FastifyRequest) => {
        // optional handshake authentication (?token= or Authorization: Bearer)
        const query = request.query as { token?: string } | undefined;
        const auth = query?.token ? await verifyRemoteToken(query.token, fastify) : null;
        const initialContext: Partial<RemoteConnectionContext> | undefined = auth
            ? { userId: auth.userId, metadata: { roles: auth.roles, email: auth.email } }
            : undefined;

        remoteServer.handleConnection(socket as RemoteSocket, initialContext);
    });

    return remoteServer;
}
```

`ServerChannel`, `serverBus`, `knownChannels` and `verifyRemoteToken` are application code. Requirements on the server bus:

- `send({ channel, group?, topic?, payload? })` - receives client `MSG` frames.
- `request({ channel, group?, topic?, payload? })` - serves client `REQ` frames; resolve with a msgmesh response message (its `payload` is unwrapped) or a raw value.
- `on({ channel, topic?, options: { abortSignal }, callback })` - lets sessions listen for events they forward. Publish events with `bus.send(...)` without a group (or with `group: 'in'`) so they reach these listeners on a msgmesh bus.

### Any other socket library

Anything that can be adapted to `RemoteSocket` works, including a plain `ws` server:

```typescript
import { WebSocketServer } from 'ws';
import { RemoteMeshServer, type RemoteSocket } from '@actdim/msgmesh-remote/server';

const remoteServer = new RemoteMeshServer({ bus: serverBus });
const wss = new WebSocketServer({ port: 8080 });
wss.on('connection', (socket) => {
    remoteServer.handleConnection(socket as unknown as RemoteSocket, { connectionId: crypto.randomUUID() });
});
```

Because the frames are plain JSON objects with a `t` discriminator, a server written in another language can implement the same protocol; this package ships only the TypeScript server.

---

## 3. Client: Browser or WebView

Condensed from mempart's `apps/webapp/src/config/remoteClient.ts`:

```typescript
import { RemoteMeshClient, bridgeRemoteBus, type RemoteBusLike } from '@actdim/msgmesh-remote/client';

const client = new RemoteMeshClient({
    url: () => `${apiBaseUrl.replace(/^http/, 'ws')}/api/v1/ws`, // re-evaluated on every (re)connect
    tokenGetter: async () => {
        const auth = await appBus.request({ channel: 'APP.SECURITY.AUTH.INFO.GET', group: 'in', options: { timeout: 3000 } });
        const payload = auth?.payload as { accessToken?: string; isAuthenticated?: boolean } | undefined;
        return payload?.isAuthenticated ? payload.accessToken : undefined;
    },
    heartbeatIntervalMs: 15000,
    heartbeatTimeoutMs: 5000,
    minReconnectDelayMs: 500,
    maxReconnectDelayMs: 10000,
    maxOfflineQueueSize: 200,
});

const unbridge = bridgeRemoteBus(appBus as unknown as RemoteBusLike, client, {
    remoteSubscriptions: [
        { channel: 'WORKS.INTAKE.*' },
        { channel: 'FEED.EXCHANGE.*' },
        { channel: 'VFS.NODE.*' },
    ],
});

client.connect();

// Refresh the token in-band after the user signs in again
appBus.on({
    channel: 'APP.SECURITY.AUTH.SIGNIN',
    group: 'in',
    callback: (msg) => {
        const token = (msg.payload as { accessToken?: string } | undefined)?.accessToken;
        if (token && client.getState() === 'OPEN') {
            void client.authenticate(token).catch(() => {});
        }
    },
});
```

Bridged `MSG` frames are re-published on the local bus with `bus.send(...)`, so UI code consumes them like any local event:

```typescript
appBus.on({
    channel: 'JOBS.STATUS',
    topic: jobId,
    group: 'in',
    callback: (msg) => updateProgress(msg.payload),
});
```

### Per-topic subscriptions

Subscribe to a concrete topic for keyed streams and unsubscribe when done:

```typescript
client.subscribe('JOBS.STATUS', jobId);
// ...
client.unsubscribe('JOBS.STATUS', jobId);
```

Subscriptions survive reconnects; you do not need to resubscribe in `onStateChange`.

### Remote RPC through the local bus

List channels in `remoteRequests` to make `appBus.request(...)` on those channels go to the server:

```typescript
const unbridge = client.attachToBus(appBus as unknown as RemoteBusLike, {
    remoteRequests: ['API.REMOTE.CALL'],
});

const res = await appBus.request({ channel: 'API.REMOTE.CALL', payload: { query: 'test' } });
```

Or call the server directly:

```typescript
const doc = await client.request<{ docId: string; name: string }>('CAD.GET_DOCUMENT', { id: 'doc-001' }, { timeout: 5000 });
```

### Fire-and-forget to the server

```typescript
client.send('CAD.OBJECT_MUTATION', { id: 'obj-1', color: 'red' });
```

Sent immediately when `OPEN`, otherwise buffered and flushed after the next open.

### Connection status in UI

```typescript
const off = client.onStateChange((state) => {
    // 'CONNECTING' | 'OPEN' | 'RECONNECTING' | 'CLOSED'
    statusBadge.set(state);
});
```

### Teardown

```typescript
unbridge();     // removes local providers, message forwarding and bridge subscriptions
client.close(); // stops reconnecting, rejects pending requests, clears the offline queue
```

### Non-browser clients

In environments without a global `WebSocket`, pass `socketFactory`. If neither `url` nor `socketFactory` is usable, socket creation fails, the error is logged and the client keeps retrying with backoff.

```typescript
const client = new RemoteMeshClient({ socketFactory: () => createMySocket() });
```

A factory returning a `RemoteSocket` (with `on`) is treated as already open.

---

## 4. Testing Without a Network

All tests in `tests/` run in Node with in-memory sockets:

- `tests/integration.test.ts` builds a linked `RemoteSocket` pair (`createSocketPair()`), connects a real `RemoteMeshClient` to a real `RemoteMeshServer` with a mock bus, and covers RPC, server-to-client pub/sub and offline buffering.
- `tests/client.test.ts` and `tests/server.test.ts` use a `MockSocket` class that records `sent` frames and exposes `triggerMessage` / `receiveMessage`.

A mock bus is just an object literal, because every bus method is optional:

```typescript
const serverBus = {
    on: () => {},
    send: () => {},
    request: async (msg: { channel: string; payload?: unknown }) => ({ ok: true, channel: msg.channel }),
};
const server = new RemoteMeshServer({ bus: serverBus });
```

For raw protocol tests against a running server, use the protocol entry point (as mempart's `apps/server/src/testRemoteMeshWebSocket.ts` does):

```typescript
import { defaultCodec, createAuthFrame, createSubFrame, createPingFrame } from '@actdim/msgmesh-remote/protocol';

ws.send(defaultCodec.encode(createPingFrame()));
ws.send(defaultCodec.encode(createAuthFrame(token)));
ws.send(defaultCodec.encode(createSubFrame('JOBS.STATUS', jobId)));
```

---

## 5. Checklist

- Server bus channels that clients subscribe to with wildcards are listed in `resolveChannels`.
- Keyed streams (job ids, drive ids) are subscribed with a topic.
- `filterEvent` is set if anonymous sessions must not receive events (the default owner filter lets them through).
- `authorize` returns `true` for `PING` frames, otherwise heartbeats go unanswered and clients reconnect every cycle.
- The client is closed with `close()` on app teardown so it stops reconnecting.

---

## Document: docs/topic--05-api-reference.md (API Reference)

# API Reference

[<- Back to 04. Integration Guide](./topic--04-integration-guide.md) | [Back to Main README](../README.md)

---

## Entry Points

| Path | Source | Exports |
|---|---|---|
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote` | `src/index.ts` | `export *` from `types`, `protocol`, `server`, `client` |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/client` | `src/client.ts` | Client section below + `type RemoteBusLike` |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/server` | `src/server.ts` | Server section below + `type RemoteSocket`, `RemoteFrame`, `RemoteServerBusLike` |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/protocol` | `src/protocol.ts` | Protocol section below; values only (no type re-exports) |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-remote/types` | `src/types.ts` | Types section below (reachable through the `./*` export pattern) |

Generic parameters used throughout: `TChannel extends string = string` (channel name union), `TGroup extends string = string` (group name union, server side), `TPayload = unknown`, `TError = unknown`.

---

## Client (`@actdim/msgmesh-remote/client`)

### `class RemoteMeshClient<TChannel>`

```typescript
constructor(options: RemoteClientOptions)
readonly options: RemoteClientOptions
readonly codec: FrameCodec // options.codec ?? defaultCodec
```

| Member | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `getState` | `(): ClientConnectionState` | Current state (initially `'CLOSED'`) |
| `onStateChange` | `(listener: (state) => void): () => void` | Listen to state transitions; returns an unsubscribe function |
| `onMessage` | `(listener: (frame: RemoteMsgFrame<TChannel>) => void): () => void` | Listen to incoming `MSG` frames; listener errors are logged |
| `connect` | `(): void` | Open the socket (no-op while `OPEN` or `CONNECTING`); clears the explicit-close flag |
| `authenticate` | `(token: string, timeoutMs = 10000): Promise<void>` | Send `AUTH`; resolve on `AUTH_OK`, reject on `AUTH_FAIL` / timeout / not `OPEN` |
| `subscribe` | `(channel: TChannel, topic?: string, group?: string): void` | Register a subscription; sends `SUB` when `OPEN`, replayed on every open |
| `unsubscribe` | `(channel: TChannel, topic?: string, group?: string): void` | Remove a subscription; sends `UNSUB` when `OPEN` |
| `send` | `(channel: TChannel, payload?: unknown, topic?: string, group?: string): void` | Send `MSG`; queued while not `OPEN` |
| `request` | `<T = unknown>(channel: TChannel, payload?: unknown, options?: { topic?: string; group?: string; timeout?: number }): Promise<T>` | Correlated RPC via `REQ` / `RES` |
| `close` | `(): void` | Stop reconnecting, reject pending auth and requests, clear the queue, close the socket, state `'CLOSED'` |
| `attachToBus` | `(bus: RemoteBusLike<TChannel>, options?: RemoteBusBridgeConfig<TChannel>): () => void` | Same as `bridgeRemoteBus(bus, this, options)` |

### `function bridgeRemoteBus<TChannel>(bus, client, config?): () => void`

```typescript
function bridgeRemoteBus<TChannel extends string = string>(
    bus: RemoteBusLike<TChannel>,
    client: RemoteMeshClient<TChannel>,
    config?: RemoteBusBridgeConfig<TChannel>,
): () => void;
```

Subscribes `config.remoteSubscriptions`, forwards every incoming `MSG` to `bus.send`, registers `bus.provide` forwarders for the array form of `config.remoteRequests`. The returned function undoes all three.

### `type ClientConnectionState`

```typescript
type ClientConnectionState = 'CONNECTING' | 'OPEN' | 'RECONNECTING' | 'CLOSED';
```

### `interface RemoteClientOptions`

| Option | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string \| (() => string)` | - | WebSocket URL for the global `WebSocket`; a function is called on each connect |
| `socketFactory` | `() => WebSocket \| RemoteSocket` | - | Custom socket; takes precedence over `url` |
| `token` | `string` | - | Static token sent as `AUTH` on every open |
| `tokenGetter` | `() => string \| undefined \| Promise<string \| undefined>` | - | Token provider used when `token` is not set |
| `codec` | `FrameCodec` | `defaultCodec` | Frame serialization |
| `heartbeatIntervalMs` | `number` | `15000` | `PING` interval |
| `heartbeatTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | Max wait for `PONG` before the socket is terminated |
| `minReconnectDelayMs` | `number` | `500` | First reconnect delay (before jitter) |
| `maxReconnectDelayMs` | `number` | `10000` | Backoff cap (before jitter) |
| `maxOfflineQueueSize` | `number` | `200` | Max buffered `MSG` frames while not `OPEN` |
| `defaultRequestTimeoutMs` | `number` | `10000` | `request()` timeout when none is passed |
| `logger` | `{ debug?, info?, warn?, error? }` | - | Optional logger; each method is `(msg: string, ...args: unknown[]) => void` |

### `interface RemoteSubscriptionItem<TChannel>`

```typescript
interface RemoteSubscriptionItem<TChannel extends string = string> {
    channel: TChannel;
    topic?: string;
    group?: string;
}
```

### `interface RemoteBusBridgeConfig<TChannel>`

| Field | Type | Behavior in `bridgeRemoteBus` |
|---|---|---|
| `remoteRequests` | `TChannel[] \| ((channel: string) => boolean)` | Array: one `bus.provide` forwarder per channel. Function form: declared, not used |
| `sendToRemote` | `TChannel[] \| ((channel: string) => boolean)` | Declared, not used |
| `remoteSubscriptions` | `RemoteSubscriptionItem<TChannel>[]` | Subscribed on bridge, unsubscribed on dispose |

---

## Server (`@actdim/msgmesh-remote/server`)

### `class RemoteMeshServer<TChannel, TGroup>`

```typescript
constructor(options: RemoteServerOptions<TChannel, TGroup>)
readonly options: RemoteServerOptions<TChannel, TGroup>
readonly codec: FrameCodec // options.codec ?? defaultCodec
```

| Member | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `handleConnection` | `(socket: RemoteSocket, context?: Partial<RemoteConnectionContext>): RemoteClientSession<TChannel, TGroup>` | Create a session, decode and dispatch its frames, clean up on `close` / `error` |
| `broadcast` | `(channel: TChannel, payload?: unknown, topic?: string, group?: string): void` | Send `MSG` to every session subscribed to the address (no `filterEvent`) |
| `activeSessionsCount` | `get: number` | Number of live sessions |
| `close` | `(): void` | Close every session and its socket |

### `class RemoteClientSession<TChannel, TGroup>`

Created by `handleConnection`; one per socket.

| Member | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `context` | `readonly RemoteConnectionContext` | Connection identity; `connectionId` defaults to `conn-<random>` |
| `socket` | `readonly RemoteSocket` | Underlying socket |
| `send` | `(frame: RemoteFrame<TChannel>): void` | Encode and send a frame (no-op after `close`) |
| `isSubscribed` | `(channel: string, topic?: string, group?: string): boolean` | Wildcard-aware subscription match |
| `handleFrame` | `(frame: RemoteFrame<TChannel>): Promise<void>` | Dispatch one decoded frame (auth, authorize, `PING`, `SUB`, `UNSUB`, `MSG`, `REQ`) |
| `close` | `(): void` | Abort all bus listeners and clear subscriptions |

### `interface RemoteConnectionContext`

```typescript
interface RemoteConnectionContext {
    connectionId: string;
    userId?: string;
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### `interface RemoteServerOptions<TChannel, TGroup>`

| Option | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `bus` | `RemoteServerBusLike<TChannel, TGroup>` | Required. Target of `MSG` / `REQ`, source of forwarded events |
| `codec` | `FrameCodec` | Frame serialization (default `defaultCodec`) |
| `resolveChannels` | `(channelPattern: string) => TChannel[]` | Expand a `SUB` / `UNSUB` channel (pattern) into bus channels |
| `onAuthenticate` | `(token, context) => result \| Promise<result>` where `result` is `{ userId?, metadata? } \| boolean \| null` | Validate `AUTH` tokens |
| `authorize` | `(context, frame: RemoteFrame<TChannel>) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Gate every non-`AUTH` frame |
| `filterEvent` | `(context, channel: string, payload: unknown, topic?: string, group?: string) => boolean` | Per-session event visibility (replaces the default owner filter) |
| `logger` | `{ debug?, info?, warn?, error? }` | Optional logger |

---

## Protocol (`@actdim/msgmesh-remote/protocol`)

### Errors

| Class | Constructor | Thrown when |
|---|---|---|
| `FrameDecodeError` | `(message: string, cause?: unknown)` | Raw data is not a string / `Uint8Array`, or JSON parsing fails |
| `InvalidFrameError` | `(message: string)` | Parsed value is not a valid frame |

Messages are prefixed with `[msgmesh-remote] Frame decode error:` and `[msgmesh-remote] Invalid frame:`.

### Validation and codec

| Export | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `validateFrame` | `(data: unknown): RemoteFrame` | Check type-specific required fields; throws `InvalidFrameError` |
| `JsonFrameCodec` | `class implements FrameCodec` | `encode(frame): string`, `decode(raw: string \| Uint8Array): RemoteFrame` |
| `defaultCodec` | `JsonFrameCodec` instance | Shared default codec |

### Frame factories

Optional arguments that are `undefined` are omitted from the frame.

| Function | Signature |
|---|---|
| `createSubFrame` | `<TChannel>(channel: TChannel, topic?: string, group?: string): RemoteSubFrame<TChannel>` |
| `createUnsubFrame` | `<TChannel>(channel: TChannel, topic?: string, group?: string): RemoteUnsubFrame<TChannel>` |
| `createMsgFrame` | `<TChannel, TPayload>(channel: TChannel, payload?: TPayload, topic?: string, group?: string): RemoteMsgFrame<TChannel, TPayload>` |
| `createReqFrame` | `<TChannel, TPayload>(id: string, channel: TChannel, payload?: TPayload, topic?: string, group?: string): RemoteReqFrame<TChannel, TPayload>` |
| `createResFrame` | `<TPayload, TError>(id: string, payload?: TPayload, error?: TError): RemoteResFrame<TPayload, TError>` (if `error` is defined, `payload` is dropped) |
| `createPingFrame` | `(): RemotePingFrame` |
| `createPongFrame` | `(): RemotePongFrame` |
| `createAuthFrame` | `(token: string, metadata?: Record<string, unknown>): RemoteAuthFrame` |
| `createAuthOkFrame` | `(userId?: string): RemoteAuthOkFrame` (empty `userId` omitted) |
| `createAuthFailFrame` | `(error: string, code?: number): RemoteAuthFailFrame` |

Note the argument order: `topic` comes before `group` in every factory and in the client methods.

---

## Types (`@actdim/msgmesh-remote/types`)

| Type | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `RemoteFrameType` | union | `'SUB' \| 'UNSUB' \| 'MSG' \| 'REQ' \| 'RES' \| 'PING' \| 'PONG' \| 'AUTH' \| 'AUTH_OK' \| 'AUTH_FAIL'` |
| `RemoteSubFrame<TChannel>` | type | `{ t: 'SUB'; channel; group?; topic? }` |
| `RemoteUnsubFrame<TChannel>` | type | `{ t: 'UNSUB'; channel; group?; topic? }` |
| `RemoteMsgFrame<TChannel, TPayload>` | type | `{ t: 'MSG'; channel; group?; topic?; payload? }` |
| `RemoteReqFrame<TChannel, TPayload>` | type | `{ t: 'REQ'; id; channel; group?; topic?; payload? }` |
| `RemoteResFrame<TPayload, TError>` | type | `{ t: 'RES'; id; payload?; error? }` |
| `RemotePingFrame` / `RemotePongFrame` | type | `{ t: 'PING' }` / `{ t: 'PONG' }` |
| `RemoteAuthFrame` | type | `{ t: 'AUTH'; token; metadata? }` |
| `RemoteAuthOkFrame` | type | `{ t: 'AUTH_OK'; userId? }` |
| `RemoteAuthFailFrame` | type | `{ t: 'AUTH_FAIL'; error; code? }` |
| `RemoteFrame<TChannel, TPayload, TError>` | union | All ten frame types |
| `FrameCodec` | interface | `encode(frame): string \| Uint8Array`, `decode(raw): RemoteFrame` |
| `RemoteSocket` | interface | `send(data)`, `on('message' \| 'close' \| 'error', listener)`, `close(code?, reason?)` |
| `RemoteServerBusLike<TChannel, TGroup>` | interface | Optional `send`, `request`, `on` |
| `RemoteBusLike<TChannel, TGroup>` | interface | `RemoteServerBusLike` + optional `provide` |

Field-level details and validation rules: [Domain Model](./topic--domain-model.md).

## Document: docs/topic--architecture.md (Architecture)

# @actdim/msgmesh-remote Architecture

## 1. System Overview

`@actdim/msgmesh-remote` bridges two `@actdim/msgmesh` buses over a duplex socket. It is layered so that each layer can be used on its own: the protocol layer has no runtime state, the server and client depend only on the protocol layer and on structural "bus-like" and "socket" interfaces.

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                  @actdim/msgmesh-remote                                   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Type Contracts (src/types.ts, zero runtime)                                              |
|  - RemoteFrame union: SUB, UNSUB, MSG, REQ, RES, PING, PONG, AUTH, AUTH_OK, AUTH_FAIL     |
|  - FrameCodec, RemoteSocket, RemoteServerBusLike, RemoteBusLike                           |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Protocol (src/protocol.ts, entry ./protocol)                                             |
|  - validateFrame, JsonFrameCodec, defaultCodec                                            |
|  - FrameDecodeError, InvalidFrameError, create*Frame factories                            |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Server (src/server.ts, entry ./server)          |  Client (src/client.ts, entry ./client)|
|  - RemoteMeshServer: session registry,           |  - RemoteMeshClient: state machine,    |
|    broadcast, close                              |    heartbeat, backoff reconnect,       |
|  - RemoteClientSession: AUTH, authorize,         |    subscription replay, offline queue, |
|    SUB/UNSUB -> bus.on, MSG -> bus.send,         |    REQ/RES correlation, authenticate   |
|    REQ -> bus.request, event filtering           |  - bridgeRemoteBus / attachToBus       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Host integration (application code)                                                      |
|  - Server: WebSocket route (e.g. @fastify/websocket) -> server.handleConnection(socket)   |
|  - Client: local msgmesh bus <- bridgeRemoteBus -> RemoteMeshClient(url | socketFactory) |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## 2. Core Architectural Principles

### 2.1. Same Addressing on Both Sides
Frames carry msgmesh's `channel` / `group` / `topic` address verbatim. The server translates frames into `bus.send`, `bus.request` and `bus.on` calls; the client bridge translates incoming `MSG` frames into `bus.send` and local `bus.provide` calls into `REQ` frames.

### 2.2. Structural Dependencies Only
The runtime never imports `@actdim/msgmesh`. It calls optional methods on `RemoteServerBusLike` / `RemoteBusLike` and on a duck-typed `RemoteSocket`, so hosts can use any socket library and tests can use object literals.

### 2.3. Client Owns Resilience
Liveness detection (`PING` / `PONG`), reconnect backoff, subscription replay and offline buffering live in the client. The server is reactive: it answers `PING` and cleans up a session when its socket emits `close` or `error`.

### 2.4. Server Owns Policy
Identity (handshake context, `onAuthenticate`), access control (`authorize`) and event visibility (`filterEvent` or the default owner filter) are server-side hooks evaluated per session.

## 3. Detailed Flows

Sequence diagrams for connect/auth, RPC, pub/sub, fire-and-forget and heartbeat are in [03. Architecture & Wiring](./topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md).

## 4. Cross-Links

- [Knowledge Base Index](./INDEX.md) - Knowledge Base Root

- [Core Concepts](./topic--02-core-concepts.md) - Addressing, frames, lifecycle, auth

## Document: docs/topic--domain-model.md (Domain Model)

# @actdim/msgmesh-remote Domain Model & Protocol Contracts

## 1. Domain Overview

The domain of `@actdim/msgmesh-remote` is the **wire frame**: a JSON object discriminated by `t`. Around it sit the contracts for serialization (`FrameCodec`), transport (`RemoteSocket`), the buses on each side (`RemoteServerBusLike`, `RemoteBusLike`) and the server's per-connection identity (`RemoteConnectionContext`). All types live in `src/types.ts` except `RemoteConnectionContext` (`src/server.ts`) and the client option types (`src/client.ts`).

## 2. Frames

### 2.1. Subscription frames (client -> server)

```typescript
type RemoteSubFrame<TChannel extends string = string> = {
    t: 'SUB';
    channel: TChannel;
    group?: string;
    topic?: string;
};

type RemoteUnsubFrame<TChannel extends string = string> = {
    t: 'UNSUB';
    channel: TChannel;
    group?: string;
    topic?: string;
};
```

`channel` may be a pattern (`'*'` or a trailing `*` prefix); `topic` / `group` may be `'*'`. Example: `{ "t": "SUB", "channel": "JOBS.STATUS", "topic": "job-42" }`.

### 2.2. Message frame (both directions)

```typescript
type RemoteMsgFrame<TChannel extends string = string, TPayload = unknown> = {
    t: 'MSG';
    channel: TChannel;
    group?: string;
    topic?: string;
    payload?: TPayload;
};
```

Client -> server: forwarded to `bus.send`. Server -> client: an event the session is subscribed to.

### 2.3. RPC frames

```typescript
type RemoteReqFrame<TChannel extends string = string, TPayload = unknown> = {
    t: 'REQ';
    id: string;
    channel: TChannel;
    group?: string;
    topic?: string;
    payload?: TPayload;
};

type RemoteResFrame<TPayload = unknown, TError = unknown> = {
    t: 'RES';
    id: string;
    payload?: TPayload;
    error?: TError;
};
```

`id` correlates a `RES` with its `REQ`. A `RES` has either `payload` or `error`. Error payloads produced by the server:

| Situation | `error` value |
|---|---|
| `authorize` denied a `REQ` | `{ message: 'Unauthorized', code: 403 }` |
| Server bus has no `request` | `{ message: 'Server bus has no request provider' }` |
| `bus.request` threw an `Error` | `{ message, name, ...ownEnumerableProps }` |
| `bus.request` threw a non-`Error` object | its own enumerable properties |
| `bus.request` threw a primitive | `{ message: String(err) }` |

### 2.4. Heartbeat frames

```typescript
type RemotePingFrame = { t: 'PING' };
type RemotePongFrame = { t: 'PONG' };
```

Either side answers `PING` with `PONG`; only the client sends `PING` on a timer.

### 2.5. Authentication frames

```typescript
type RemoteAuthFrame = { t: 'AUTH'; token: string; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> };
type RemoteAuthOkFrame = { t: 'AUTH_OK'; userId?: string };
type RemoteAuthFailFrame = { t: 'AUTH_FAIL'; error: string; code?: number };
```

Server codes: `401` for a falsy `onAuthenticate` result, `500` when `onAuthenticate` throws. `RemoteAuthFrame.metadata` is part of the frame contract; the server's `handleAuth` passes only `token` and the session context to `onAuthenticate`, and the client's automatic and explicit `AUTH` frames carry no metadata.

### 2.6. Union and type tag

```typescript
type RemoteFrameType = 'SUB' | 'UNSUB' | 'MSG' | 'REQ' | 'RES' | 'PING' | 'PONG' | 'AUTH' | 'AUTH_OK' | 'AUTH_FAIL';

type RemoteFrame<TChannel extends string = string, TPayload = unknown, TError = unknown> =
    | RemoteSubFrame<TChannel>
    | RemoteUnsubFrame<TChannel>
    | RemoteMsgFrame<TChannel, TPayload>
    | RemoteReqFrame<TChannel, TPayload>
    | RemoteResFrame<TPayload, TError>
    | RemotePingFrame
    | RemotePongFrame
    | RemoteAuthFrame
    | RemoteAuthOkFrame
    | RemoteAuthFailFrame;
```

## 3. Validation Rules (`validateFrame`)

| `t` | Required | Optional, type-checked |
|---|---|---|
| `SUB`, `UNSUB`, `MSG` | `channel`: non-empty string | `group`, `topic`: string |
| `REQ` | `id`, `channel`: non-empty strings | `group`, `topic`: string |
| `RES` | `id`: non-empty string | - |
| `PING`, `PONG` | - | (returned as a fresh `{ t }` object; extra fields dropped) |
| `AUTH` | `token`: non-empty string | - |
| `AUTH_OK` | - | - |
| `AUTH_FAIL` | `error`: non-empty string | - |

Anything else (non-object, missing or unknown `t`) throws `InvalidFrameError`. `payload`, `error`, `metadata`, `userId` and `code` are not type-checked; other frames are returned as received, extra fields included.

## 4. Infrastructure Contracts

### 4.1. `FrameCodec`

```typescript
interface FrameCodec {
    encode(frame: RemoteFrame): string | Uint8Array;
    decode(raw: string | Uint8Array): RemoteFrame;
}
```

### 4.2. `RemoteSocket`

```typescript
interface RemoteSocket {
    send(data: string | Uint8Array): void;
    on(event: 'message', listener: (data: unknown) => void): void;
    on(event: 'close', listener: (code?: number, reason?: string) => void): void;
    on(event: 'error', listener: (err: unknown) => void): void;
    close(code?: number, reason?: string): void;
}
```

### 4.3. Bus-like contracts

```typescript
interface RemoteServerBusLike<TChannel extends string = string, TGroup extends string = string> {
    send?(msg: { channel: TChannel; group?: TGroup; topic?: string; payload?: unknown }): Promise<unknown> | void;
    request?(msg: { channel: TChannel; group?: TGroup; topic?: string; payload?: unknown }): Promise<unknown>;
    on?(params: {
        channel: TChannel;
        group?: TGroup;
        topic?: string;
        options?: { abortSignal?: AbortSignal };
        callback: (msg: {
            address?: { channel: string; group?: string; topic?: string };
            channel?: string;
            group?: string;
            topic?: string;
            payload?: unknown;
        }) => void;
    }): (() => void) | void;
}

interface RemoteBusLike<TChannel extends string = string, TGroup extends string = string>
    extends RemoteServerBusLike<TChannel, TGroup> {
    provide?(params: {
        channel: TChannel;
        group?: TGroup;
        callback: (inMsg: {
            address?: { channel: string; group?: string; topic?: string };
            channel?: string;
            topic?: string;
            group?: string;
            payload?: unknown;
        }) => Promise<unknown> | unknown;
    }): (() => void) | void;
}
```

Callbacks accept both msgmesh messages (address under `address`) and flat objects (address fields at top level).

### 4.4. `RemoteConnectionContext`

```typescript
interface RemoteConnectionContext {
    connectionId: string;          // handshake value or generated 'conn-<random>'
    userId?: string;               // handshake value, replaced by onAuthenticate
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown>; // handshake value, shallow-merged by onAuthenticate
}
```

## 5. Runtime Entities

| Entity | Lifetime | Key state |
|---|---|---|
| `RemoteMeshServer` | Application | Set of live sessions |
| `RemoteClientSession` | One socket | `context`, subscriptions (`channel::group::topic`), bus listeners (`busChannel::topic` -> abort) |
| `RemoteMeshClient` | Application | `ClientConnectionState`, subscription registry (`channel::group::topic`), offline `MSG` queue, pending requests by `id`, pending auth, heartbeat and reconnect timers |
| Bridge disposer | Until called | Message listener, `provide` disposers, bridge subscriptions |

## 6. Cross-Links

- [Knowledge Base Index](./INDEX.md) - Knowledge Base Root

- [Core Concepts](./topic--02-core-concepts.md) - How the frames are used

## Document: docs/topic--setup-and-workflow.md (Setup And Workflow)

# @actdim/msgmesh-remote Setup, Build & Test Workflow

## 1. Repository Layout

`@actdim/msgmesh-remote` has its own Git repository (`https://github.com/actdim/msgmesh-remote`) and is developed as a Git submodule of the mempart monorepo at `src/packages/msgmesh-remote`. The monorepo's pnpm workspace (`src/pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `packages/*` and `apps/*`) links it with its sibling `@actdim/msgmesh` (`src/packages/msgmesh`) and with the consumers `apps/server` and `apps/webapp`.

```text
msgmesh-remote/
|-- src/            index.ts, types.ts, protocol.ts, server.ts, client.ts
|-- tests/          protocol, server, client and integration Vitest suites
|-- docs/           Knowledge Base (this folder) and the VitePress site config
|-- packageConfig.ts         aliases, source file list and peer externals for Vite / Vitest
|-- vite.config.ts           library build (ESM, preserveModules, .d.ts via vite-plugin-dts)
|-- vitest.node.config.ts    Node test configuration
|-- tsconfig*.json           base / build / dev project references
```

## 2. Prerequisites & Installation

- **Package manager**: `pnpm` (the mempart workspace pins `pnpm@10.30.3`)
- **TypeScript**: `^5.9.3`

Inside the monorepo, install from `src/`:

```bash
pnpm install
```

Peer dependencies for consumers:

```bash
pnpm add @actdim/msgmesh-remote @actdim/msgmesh rxjs
```

## 3. Scripts

Run from the package folder (`src/packages/msgmesh-remote`):

| Command | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm run build` | `tsc -b tsconfig.json && vite build` | Typecheck, then emit ESM modules (`dist/<module>.es.js`) and declarations (`dist/<module>.d.ts`) |
| `pnpm run typecheck` | `tsc -b tsconfig.json` | Typecheck only |
| `pnpm run test` | `npx vitest --config=vitest.node.config.ts --no-cache` | Run all `tests/**/*.test.ts` once in Node |
| `pnpm run test:w` | `npx vitest --config=vitest.node.config.ts --watch` | Watch mode |
| `pnpm run format` | `prettier --write .` | Format |
| `pnpm run format:check` | `prettier --check .` | Check formatting |
| `pnpm run docs:dev` | `vitepress dev docs` | Local docs site |
| `pnpm run docs:build` | `vitepress build docs` | Build the docs site (GitHub Pages: https://actdim.github.io/msgmesh-remote/) |
| `pnpm run docs:preview` | `vitepress preview docs` | Preview the built docs |

From the monorepo root (`src/`), `pnpm build` runs every workspace package's `build` script, including this one.

## 4. Test Suites

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `tests/protocol.test.ts` | Encode/decode of every frame type, `Uint8Array` input, invalid JSON, unknown type, missing fields |
| `tests/server.test.ts` | `PING` -> `PONG`, `AUTH` success/failure, `REQ` -> `RES`, wildcard channel subscriptions, default tenant isolation, cleanup on close |
| `tests/client.test.ts` | `AUTH` on open, `authenticate()` resolve/reject, heartbeat and dead-socket termination, offline queue flush, `bridgeRemoteBus` |
| `tests/integration.test.ts` | Real client and server over an in-memory socket pair: RPC, pub/sub, offline buffering |

The client tests use Vitest fake timers; all suites are hermetic (no network).

Mempart also exercises the package end to end against a real Fastify WebSocket server in `apps/server/src/testRemoteMeshWebSocket.ts` and against the app bus in `apps/webapp/tests/remoteClient.test.ts`.

## 5. Versioning & Release

The mempart monorepo uses one synchronized version for all apps, packages and submodules. The package version (currently `1.12.0`) is never bumped in isolation: run `pnpm run version:sync <version>` from mempart's `src/` (it updates this package's `package.json` together with the others), then commit, tag `vX.Y.Z` and push the root repository and all submodules together. The `@actdim/msgmesh` peer range tracks the same version line (`>=1.12.0`).

The published tarball contains `dist`, `docs` (without `docs/.vitepress`), `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` (see `files` in `package.json`).
